# PanCode

> PanCode is one harness for the models and coding agents you already use. Panos, its orchestrator agent, routes work across providers, sandboxes commands, checks finished work against what ran, keeps memory and runs fleets of workers, in the terminal, in scripts and CI, in ACP editors and on the desktop (alpha). It installs on HPC login nodes without root and ships checks for numerical work.

PanCode is a harness for development work. Panos, its orchestrator agent, plans a task, runs it on the models you connect and hands parts of it to workers, including the coding agents you already have. It routes across providers, sandboxes commands, checks finished work against what ran and keeps memory, in the terminal, in scripts and CI, in ACP editors or on the desktop. PanHub packs and PanKit servers cover HPC and scientific software.

PanCode is a product of PanStudio. It needs no account and no root, and sends nothing home. It is free for individuals, small organizations (fewer than 100 people and under $1M revenue), and noncommercial research and teaching. Its source is available on GitHub under the PanCode License 1.0. Larger organizations get a 32-day evaluation, then a commercial license from PanStudio.

- Install on macOS, Linux, or WSL: `curl -fsSL https://pancode.dev/install.sh | sh`
- Install on Windows (best effort) in PowerShell: `irm https://pancode.dev/install.ps1 | iex`
- Install with npm (Node.js 22.19 or newer): `npm install -g @panstudio/pancode`
- Connect a model in a project: `pancode configure`; then run `pancode` for the terminal or `pancode gui --open` for the desktop alpha.
- Current release: v0.9.1. Source: https://github.com/PanStudio/pancode. License: PanCode License 1.0.

## Start

- [Install PanCode](https://pancode.dev/docs.html): Install, update, and launch PanCode on your machine.
- [Install on a cluster](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/hpc-clusters.html): Install PanCode on a login node with an old glibc, a proxy, or no internet.
- [Connect a model](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/configuration-and-targets.html): Set up local models, institutional endpoints, and cloud connections.

## Everyday use

- [Commands and shortcuts](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/commands-and-modes.html): Navigate the terminal, choose models, and control a session.
- [Tools and permissions](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/tool-usage.html): Read, search, edit, and run commands with PanCode's repository tools.
- [Sandbox and safety](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/sandbox-and-safety.html): What a sandboxed command may do, what it hides, and when PanCode asks you.
- [Save and resume work](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/context-continuity.html): Resume conversations, manage context, and prepare a handoff.
- [Memory and lessons](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/proactive-memory.html): See what PanCode remembers, approve lessons, or turn memory off.
- [Files and terminal panes](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/panes-and-files.html): Attach files and open companion terminal panes.
- [The desktop app](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/gui.html): Open the desktop alpha, keep tasks in one window, and read the Session column.
- [Require project checks](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/quality-policy.html): Choose the declared checks a change requires and inspect verification freshness.
- [Climb a metric, compare models](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/research-and-arena.html): Improve a measured number with verified research campaigns, and compare models blind in the arena.
- [Automate with pancode run](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/exit-codes-and-output.html): Run one task from a script or CI job, read its exit code, and parse its JSON output.
- [Semantic context](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/semantic-context.html): Search your project by meaning with a local embedding route.
- [Built-in and custom agents](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/built-in-agents.html): See the agents you can dispatch and add your own.

## Store, hub and toolkit

- [Keep results in PanStore](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/panstore.html): Keep datasets and results outside the working tree, with a record of where each came from.
- [Packs from PanHub](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/panhub.html): Find, install and manage skills, plugins, extensions and other packs.
- [Tool servers with PanKit](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/pankit.html): Run PanKit's MCP tool servers in PanCode or in any other MCP host.

## Extend PanCode

- [Workers and fleets](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/fleet-dispatch.html): Assign focused tasks and combine workers into a workflow.
- [Install plugins](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/plugins.html): Add reusable resources to your PanCode installation.
- [Write and install extensions](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/harness-extensions.html): Install and write extensions that declare what they may do.
- [Extension API (unstable)](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/sdk.html): Scaffold, validate and test extensions, and write MCP tool servers.
- [Editors and other agents](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/interop.html): Use supported agent connections and editor integrations.

## Reference

- [Check your installation](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/doctor.html): Diagnose installation and connection problems with doctor.
- [Troubleshooting](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/troubleshooting.html): Resolve common connection, terminal, and runtime problems.
- [Configuration essentials](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/configuration-reference.html): Find settings layers, save scopes, and the full configuration reference.
- [Environment essentials](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/environment-variables.html): Use directory overrides and existing provider credentials when needed.
- [System One decision models](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/system-one.html): Bring a decision model, name a route, and read its limits.
- [Information flow](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/information-flow.html): Keep named files away from destinations you did not choose.
- [Glossary](https://pancode.dev/docs/guide/glossary.html): Plain-language meanings of the words PanCode uses, from target to worktree.

## PanHub

- [PanHub](https://pancode.dev/hub.html): The PanHub marketplace: every pack in the index bundled with this PanCode release, with its tier, licence, source and the command that installs or serves it.

## Tutorials

- [Your first session with PanCode](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/first-session.html): Connect a model, open a repository, and ask PanCode to explain how it builds and runs its tests.
- [Desktop or terminal: find your workspace](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/desktop-and-terminal.html): See both interfaces, learn how to launch them, and choose where to start your next coding session.
- [Let PanCode work without watching every call](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/let-it-work-with-containment-and-rewind.html): Check the sandbox, undo a change with /rewind, tell the safety judge about your machine, and know when yolo is the right call.
- [Run a playbook from plan to commit](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/run-a-playbook-and-land-it.html): Run the built-in sdlc playbook on one task, watch it work, and read the three commits it makes on your branch.
- [Run it unattended within limits](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/run-it-unattended-within-limits.html): Start a headless run with a cost ceiling and a timeout, ask read-only questions, schedule turns, and know what stops each one.
- [Script PanCode in CI](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/script-pancode-in-ci.html): Build a CI job on one JSON result, typed exit codes, run limits, a dry run, and an answer validated against your schema.
- [See what a session cost and what a run did](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/see-what-a-session-cost-and-what-a-run-did.html): Read session cost and stop reasons from local journals, verify a sealed record, and prepare an archive that uploads nothing.
- [A numerical change, checked with PanCode](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/temperature-calibration.html): Follow a temperature-conversion example through a floating-point test failure, a correction, and recorded verification.
- [Choose a model for your project](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/choose-model-for-your-project.html): Connect a local server, a cloud API, or a supported subscription route, then choose models separately for conversation and delegated work.
- [Coordinate the coding agents you already use](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/coordinate-your-coding-agents.html): Hand a bounded task to a coding agent you have installed, tell a managed run from an interactive handoff, and review what comes back before you combine it.
- [Keep a long coding task on track](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/keep-long-coding-tasks-on-track.html): See what fills the context, carry your decisions through a handoff, and resume the right branch of a long task.
- [Check a change against your repository](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/check-a-change-against-your-repository.html): Name the checks that matter, run them through verify, and see whether a passing result still matches the files you are reviewing.
- [Add skills and plugins deliberately](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/add-skills-and-plugins-deliberately.html): Preview a project skill or plugin, inspect its package pin, and load only what your task needs; installing is not a permission grant.
- [Work from a laptop with remote workers](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/work-from-a-laptop-with-remote-workers.html): Coordinate workers on other machines over SSH from your laptop, once each node has the same PanCode version and the project at the same path.
- [Write an extension with declared capabilities](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/write-an-extension-with-declared-capabilities.html): Scaffold, test, and install a small extension, and see exactly what approving its capabilities covers.
- [Diffusion models in the terminal](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/diffusion-models.html): Connect Inception's Mercury models for chat and workers, and watch an answer refine as a whole instead of arriving token by token.
- [Panes and docks: files, workers, and music](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/panes-and-docks.html): Show and hide a file browser, a live worker dashboard, and a focus radio beside the terminal conversation with one key each.
- [Keep named files with the models you chose](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/information-flow-rules.html): Declare which paths and tool results may reach which model targets, approve the policy, and see a request to any other destination refused.
- [Search by meaning and record worker runs](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/semantic-context-and-recordings.html): Index code, memory, and experiment folders with a local embedding model, and attach a redacted terminal recording to a worker's evidence.
- [Run PanCode on a local model](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/run-on-a-local-model.html): Connect a local server with no account or key, check what PanCode learned about it, and see what else to check if code must stay on your machine.
- [Pre-register a benchmark before you measure](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/pre-register-a-benchmark.html): Use the experiment-protocol skill to lock thresholds, tolerances, and verdict conditions into a contract you commit before any result exists.
- [Keep results outside the tree with the project store](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/keep-results-in-the-project-store.html): Store a result with a note, check it for drift, read it from a script, and let a worker write into one granted tag.
- [Set up a lab from one setup file](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/set-up-a-lab-from-one-setup-file.html): Write one YAML file that connects every lab member to your model gateway, check what it may carry, and test the route.
- [Share a folder with a teammate or a second terminal](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/share-a-folder-with-a-teammate-or-a-second-terminal.html): Run two sessions in one project, keep each person's state private, and commit project settings that can only make PanCode stricter.
- [Run a research campaign and a blind arena](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/run-a-research-campaign-and-a-blind-arena.html): Keep a speed-up only when a measurement proves it and the answers still match, then compare model answers without knowing which model wrote them.
- [Report a problem without leaking your machine](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/report-a-problem-without-leaking-your-machine.html): Draft a bug report, read the exact text with your paths, names and keys masked, choose how it leaves, and share a diagnostic bundle only if you want to.
- [Ask several agents at once](https://pancode.dev/tutorials/ask-several-agents-at-once.html): Poll two to five agents on one question and read the vote, or give a council roster one task and let a judge write a single answer.

## Research

- [Drivers: the model you have, on its own wire](https://pancode.dev/research/drivers.html): How PanCode shapes each request for its provider wire, names the cause of a cache break, and an experiment to measure the saving.
- [Memory: context as a priced storage tier](https://pancode.dev/research/memory.html): How PanCode tiers the context window, prices an eviction against the prompt cache, and recalls evicted output exactly, with a first experiment.
- [Scheduling: a mixed fleet under one policy](https://pancode.dev/research/scheduling.html): How PanCode admits, bounds, and grades its workers and other coding agents, with a first experiment against a single agent.
- [Protection: a floor at every autonomy level](https://pancode.dev/research/protection.html): How PanCode decides each call: a fixed floor, containment, a judge that never reads model text, and flow rules, with a first experiment.
- [Accounting: done, checked against what ran](https://pancode.dev/research/accounting.html): How PanCode checks a finished task against what it observed and seals the record, with the first experiment the project plans to run.
- [Can a small decision model improve an agent's work?](https://pancode.dev/research/system-one-decisions.html): Open questions on System One: evaluating on trajectories, asking better questions, and bringing a decision model, with a first experiment.
- [Can an agent run be a scientific record?](https://pancode.dev/research/sealed-run-records.html): What a sealed run record proves and what it cannot, how far repeated runs differ, and a first experiment to measure that spread with PanCode.
- [Does agent memory change outcomes?](https://pancode.dev/research/proactive-memory.html): Whether lessons change what an agent does, whether self-approval is safe, and a first experiment on one repeated mistake.
- [What does an agent lose when its context is reduced?](https://pancode.dev/research/context-and-retrieval.html): Fidelity of summaries, the cost of reduction, and search by meaning, with a first experiment that counts how many planted facts survive.
- [When do several agents or small models pay off?](https://pancode.dev/research/fleets-and-local-models.html): Compete, council, heterogeneous fleets and local models, with no comparative numbers yet and a first experiment on one seeded bug.
- [What would make a scientist trust an agent's change?](https://pancode.dev/research/scientific-and-hpc-workflows.html): Pre-registered checks, validated modernization, a project store and scheduler use on scientific code, with a first experiment on catching a numerical error.
